title: To amend title 38, United States Code, to clarify the role of doctors of podiatric medicine in the Department of Veterans Affairs, and for other purposes.
official_summary: This bill generally aligns the position of podiatrists with that of physicians for pay and grade purposes within the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). Additionally, the bill replaces the Director of Podiatric Service position with a Podiatric Medical Director to be responsible for the operation of the podiatric service at the VHA. Such director must be a qualified doctor of podiatric medicine.

summary.headline: A 2022 law changes how Department of Veterans Affairs podiatrists are paid and graded and renames their top leadership job.
summary.what_it_does: The law puts VA podiatrists on the same pay and grade footing as physicians within the Veterans Health Administration. It also replaces the Director of Podiatric Service position with a Podiatric Medical Director. That director must be a qualified doctor of podiatric medicine and is responsible for running the VA's podiatry service.

who_it_affects.group: Doctors of podiatric medicine (podiatrists) working for the VA
who_it_affects.how: They are placed on the same pay and grade basis as VA physicians.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans who receive foot and ankle care through the VA
who_it_affects.how: The VA's podiatry service is now run by a podiatric medical director who must be a podiatrist.
